study: Round numbers: is a new intraday high that sits just BELOW a whole or half dollar more likely to fail, and one that has just cleared a round number more likely to run (Ross Cameron's 'apex point vs psychological resistance')?
registered_at: 2026-10-08 12:16 ET (commit 0a50484); amended 13:34 ET (commit 0f55822) before any script or data
origin: Operator 10/8 (Warrior Trading transcript): 'if the apex point is 4.95 that presents a problem because the breakout spot is just below psychological resistance ... we'd rather have the apex point right at it or just above it'. Never tested here.
prior: LOW to MODERATE: round-number clustering of orders is documented in the academic literature; whether it moves 30-min outcomes on liquid $10+ names after costs is untested.
events_and_data: EXACTLY the events, universe, data, entry, exits, costs, beta hedge, clustering, halves and quote rules of name_history_prereg.json (new session-high events 10:30-15:00 on top-400 $10+ names; hedged net30 primary) - computed by the same tool on the same sessions, so the two studies share one data pull.
round_levels: primary grid by the event close: $0.50 steps under $50; $1 steps $50-100; $5 steps at $100 and above. (Other grids: information only.)

groups.BELOW: the nearest grid level strictly ABOVE the event close is within 0.15% of the close. BELOW takes precedence over ABOVE.
groups.ABOVE: not BELOW, and a grid level L satisfies H_prev < L <= close, where H_prev = the RTH session high through t-1 (the level the event broke); a close exactly on a level is ABOVE
groups.NEUTRAL: neither (the three groups are exclusive and exhaustive)

primary: ABOVE minus BELOW, hedged net30: OLS with session, event-hour and PRICE-BAND ($10-20, $20-50, $50-100, $100+) fixed effects and log(close / H_prev) as a covariate, two-way clustered (session, name) t; halves = alternate sessions. Base rates of each group per price band reported.
pass: difference >= +5 bp, one-sided two-way t >= the 1.96 equivalent at the smaller cluster df (one hypothesis), same sign in both halves, the ABOVE group's hedged net30 > 0 after costs, ABOVE beats its same-name random-minute control (name_history's control rule; else the PASS is labelled RELATIVE ONLY), robust to dropping the top 5 names and top 3 sessions; FAIL if t <= -2 or if powered (MDE <= 10 bp in both halves) and not passed; else UNDERPOWERED. A PASS needs the name_history earlier-period and IEX reruns (same bars) before a forward test.
information_only: BELOW minus NEUTRAL and ABOVE minus NEUTRAL
whole dollars only vs half dollars only
no_retuning: levels, the 0.15% band, groups and the bar fixed here
tool: tools/studies/name_history.py (round-number cells added before it scores anything; same skeptic code review)
power: OUTCOME-BLIND COUNT STEP before any outcome: n and distinct names per group per half; MDE = (t_crit + 0.84) x the projected two-way SE (from the same-name control arm of name_history, scaled to the ABOVE and BELOW group sizes); UNDERPOWERED if MDE > 10 bp in either half; if powered and not passed, FAIL.
dependence: the groups are computed and FROZEN in the same run before any name_history outcome is read; the name_history verdict does not gate this verdict; the report notes the overlap with name_history H1/H2 samples
amended: 2026-10-08 13:34 ET (commit 0f55822), before any script or data: skeptic review - exclusive groups with precedence; price-scaled primary grid; price-band FE and breakout-size covariate; H_prev defined; own outcome-blind count step; frozen groups and no gating; same-name control requirement.
